label: Computing F from Correspondences
notes: This chapter, printed pages 279 through 309, turns noisy point matches into a usable rank-two fundamental matrix. Stress that F is not just a three by three array but the output of a computation whose conditioning, rank constraint, and outlier handling each decide whether the recovered epipolar geometry can be trusted.

label: The Epipolar Constraint
notes: Open with the single algebraic fact the whole chapter rests on: every correspondence satisfies x-prime transpose F x equals zero. Show that this bilinear identity is linear in the nine entries of F, so each match supplies exactly one homogeneous equation. That observation is what makes a direct linear solution possible.

label: The Linear Eight-Point Algorithm
notes: Stack the per-correspondence rows into a design matrix A and solve A f equals zero by SVD, taking the singular vector of the smallest singular value. Emphasize that eight points fix the scale-free nine-vector, but the raw solution ignores the singularity of F and is sensitive to coordinate scaling.

label: Why Normalization Matters
notes: Raw pixel coordinates run into the hundreds, so columns of A differ by orders of magnitude and the SVD wastes precision on units. Hartley normalization translates each image's centroid to the origin and scales the RMS radius to root two, dramatically lowering the condition number before the null vector is trusted.

label: The Normalized Eight-Point Pipeline
notes: Walk the four-stage pipeline: normalize each image by a similarity T, solve the linear system by SVD, enforce rank two, then denormalize with T-prime transpose F T. The notebook measures the conditioning improvement factor at over one hundred thousand, which is the whole reason normalization is mandatory, not optional.

label: Enforcing the Rank-2 Constraint
notes: The linear estimate is generally full rank, but a true fundamental matrix is singular so that all epipolar lines meet at the epipole. Take the SVD, set the smallest singular value to zero, and reconstruct. This Frobenius-closest singular matrix is what restores a consistent epipole and pencil of epipolar lines.

label: The 7-Point Algorithm
notes: With only seven correspondences the linear system has a two-dimensional null space spanning F1 and F2. Impose the singularity constraint det of alpha F1 plus one minus alpha F2 equals zero, a cubic in alpha. The real roots give one or three candidate fundamental matrices that are already rank two by construction.

label: Algebraic vs Geometric Error
notes: Contrast the algebraic residual minimized by the linear method with geometrically meaningful error measured in pixels. The reprojection error is the gold standard; the Sampson distance is its first-order approximation, cheap to evaluate and the practical residual used to judge whether a point lies near its epipolar line.

label: The Gold-Standard MLE
notes: Under Gaussian noise the maximum-likelihood estimate minimizes total reprojection error over a consistent camera pair and a set of estimated 3D points. Parameterize through cameras so F stays rank two automatically, initialize from the normalized eight-point result, and refine with Levenberg-Marquardt. Sampson error gives a fast surrogate objective.

label: Robust Estimation with RANSAC
notes: Real match sets contain mismatches that break least squares. RANSAC samples minimal seven or eight point subsets, fits F, scores correspondences by Sampson distance against a pixel threshold, and keeps the hypothesis with the most inliers. The notebook recovers a clean inlier set with median residuals far below the rejected outliers.

label: The Automatic Computation Pipeline
notes: Assemble the full automatic method: detect features and form tentative matches, run RANSAC to estimate F and label inliers, perform guided matching along the recovered epipolar lines to grow the correspondence set, then refine F by the gold-standard cost. Iterate guided matching and refinement until the inlier set stabilizes.

label: Degeneracies and Takeaways
notes: Close on the planar degeneracy: coplanar points are explained by a homography and leave a larger design-matrix null space, so many fundamental matrices fit almost equally well. Recap the recipe of normalize, solve, enforce rank two, score robustly, and refine, and warn that rectification magnifies a poorly identified epipole.
